### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. congenital nephrotic syndrome, Finnish type  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.476)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373753)

**Proposed mechanism:** CD2AP (HGNC:2144) —DISRUPTS→ podocyte actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0001891); podocyte actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0001891) —LEADS_TO→ Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (HP:0000070); NPHS1 (HGNC:8033) —DISRUPTS→ podocyte filtration barrier integrity (GO:0007155); podocyte filtration barrier integrity (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital nephrotic syndrome (HP:0011376); podocyte actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0001891) —BINDS→ podocyte filtration barrier integrity (GO:0007155). Loss-of-function mutations in CD2AP disrupt podocyte actin cytoskeleton organization, contributing to FSGS. Loss-of-function mutations in NPHS1 disrupt the podocyte filtration barrier integrity. The actin cytoskeleton is crucial for maintaining the structure and function of the filtration barrier, creating a mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that CD2AP and NPHS1 do not functionally interact or converge on the same downstream pathways within podocytes, or that mutations in CD2AP do not affect the structural integrity of the podocyte filtration barrier, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in CD2AP or NPHS1 associated with reduced penetrance or absence of either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CD2AP and NPHS1 in maintaining podocyte filtration barrier integrity could reveal common therapeutic targets for both FSGS and congenital nephrotic syndromes, potentially involving strategies to stabilize the actin cytoskeleton or enhance nephrin function.

#### 2. ovarian cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.420)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373753)

**Proposed mechanism:** PIK3CA (HGNC:9535) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP557); AKT1 (HGNC:390) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP557); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP557) —LEADS_TO→ Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (MONDO:0011917); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP557) —LEADS_TO→ Ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170). Gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA or AKT1 lead to hyperactivation of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway. This aberrant signaling contributes to the pathogenesis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and promotes the development and progression of ovarian cancer.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of activating mutations in PIK3CA or AKT1 in patients with either focal segmental glomerulosclerosis or ovarian cancer, or demonstration that these mutations do not lead to hyperactivation of the PI3K-Akt pathway in relevant cellular models. _(variant: rs113821859)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the PI3K-Akt pathway with inhibitors could offer a therapeutic strategy for both focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and ovarian cancer, although careful patient stratification based on specific pathway alterations would be necessary.
